headline: High risk: Gemini CLI can write/egress by default while Botpress is undocumented for shared I/O, creating dangerous interaction and compliance uncertainty.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write repo files and use MCP servers, so if Botpress outputs are placed in a shared workspace or MCP channel, prompt-like content could be reinterpreted. Botpress docs do not show a shared channel, so the pathway is inferred rather than direct. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs are copied into a shared filesystem or MCP-fed prompt stream
IF Gemini CLI is configured to ingest those files as instructions
mitigations: Keep Botpress and Gemini CLI in separate directories
Disable MCP servers unless explicitly needed
Use a read-only handoff file for Botpress outputs
Add a prompt delimiter template for any copied content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI has broad network egress and reads files in cwd, while Botpress is a customer-support agent with undocumented data handling surfaces. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive support content can flow into Gemini CLI and then out to third-party APIs. The lack of Botpress I/O detail prevents a higher confidence, not a lower severity.
conditions: IF Botpress stores customer-support transcripts or attachments in a shared cwd
IF Gemini CLI is run in that same workspace with default network access
mitigations: Separate support data from coding workspaces
Run Gemini CLI with network disabled for sensitive folders
Redact transcripts before handoff
Use a dedicated non-sensitive test workspace

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can execute shell, write files, and modify git state; Botpress can install packages. If both operate on the same repo or directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and corrupt state. Botpress lacks documented locking or concurrency controls, so the shared-write pathway is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git checkout or filesystem tree
IF Botpress installs packages while Gemini CLI edits or commits files in that tree
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Freeze git writes to one agent at a time
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Enable filesystem snapshots before edits
requires-engineering: add lock coordination around shared repos

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can act on files and shell commands, so if it consumes Botpress-generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into edits or commands. Botpress is a support agent, not a verified fact source, and no verification bridge is documented. This is a plausible default workflow risk, but not enough evidence for high.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI uses Botpress output as direct task input without review
IF the output contains incorrect instructions, code, or operational facts
mitigations: Insert a human review step before execution
Require Gemini CLI to cite source files before acting
Use a checklist for any Botpress-to-Gemini handoff
Limit Botpress output to summaries, not commands

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent, so it may handle regulated support data, while Gemini CLI explicitly sends requests to Google APIs and handles GEMINI_API_KEY. Without Botpress residency or retention details, a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. I cite both because the risk arises from their combined data flow.
conditions: IF customer-support data includes regulated personal data
IF that data is processed by Gemini CLI through Google API calls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Gemini CLI prompts
Use a DPA-approved environment for support data
Mask identifiers before transfer
Document retention and deletion rules for both tools
